correctness.rationale: For all integers J>=2, the Ferrari Fejér sine-vector maximizer reconstructs Re(delta) exactly as C|(1-z)^2 Q(-z)|^2. The coefficient correlations of the positive polynomial P(w)=(1+w)^2Q(w) yield each ordinary coefficient with strict alternating sign; uniqueness of the cosine Fourier expansion rules out missing coefficients. The triangle inequality is attained uniquely at z=-r for every radius r>0. The finite sine sum evaluates delta(-1) exactly. Boundaries J=2, r>0 and nonzero end coefficients were checked; the independently recomputed high-precision test returned VERIFY_OK 5394, but universal validity rests on the exact proof in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: Ferrari arXiv:2607.11422 Section 5.1 footnote 3 explicitly poses the all-order unit-disk maximum as an unproved conjecture, reporting only orders J=2 to 6. His Theorem 3.1 and Lemmas 4.2–4.3 provide the known extremal coefficients and Fourier real-part expression, but do not imply the all-order norm without a new step. A new strictly positive Fejér sine factor gives all ordinary symbol coefficients strict alternating signs, resolving the conjecture and strengthening it to all circular radii. Banjai arXiv:2203.00986 Section 6 gives an original truncated construction and finite-order numerical optimization, not the exact all-order extremal family norm. published-finding corpus and own-ledger comparisons found low-order exponential-kernel quadrature-weight positivity and other finite-order constructions, not a dominating statement. Unindexed or concurrent rediscoveries remain possible.
residual_risks: Novelty cannot be inferred from unsuccessful searches alone; unindexed or simultaneous all-order proofs are possible.

value.rationale: Ferrari arxiv:2607.11422 explicitly singles out the all-order disk-symbol supremum as a conjecture needed to understand optimized truncated-trapezoidal CQ symbols. Settling it for every order and proving an all-radius extremal principle yields sharp scalar contour bounds and a structural ordinary-coefficient identity even when shifted-basis coefficients change signs. The result resolves a specified open question rather than adding a routine parameter or finite table; it does not assert unproved operator-valued error bounds.
